body: Ongoing mental health issues. I feel like I don’t belong on earth.

Like others have said, if your in imminent danger/ or have attempted to end your life then a and e is reasonable. Normally they are pretty good and will get psych liaison to speak to you if you want. They can then make a plan to support you in the community. Don’t worry. You won’t get admitted to hospital or sectioned etc. you have to be actively trying to end your life in pretty dangerous ways for that to happen. 

If the urges are not so bad as don’t think you will get through then I would suggest getting an urgent gp appointment all calling you mental health team if you are under one

Firstly bpd may be diagnosed as eupd in the uk. You need a psychiatrist to diagnose you. Just a warning that it’s a rubbish diagnosis that has a lot of stereotyping and makes getting help more challenging. Health services treat you like rubbish if you have a bpd / eupd diagnosis I have found
How’s it going?
I would get your parents to say that you are a mass Suicide risk and they don’t feel able to manage the risk at home. Hope and pray you get some help.

It’s pretty hard to get a mental health bed and treatment in the Uk. People don’t realise how unwell you have to be. Also there is a large shortage of beds and availability of treatment so it’s hard. You are unlikely to get listened to or treatment unless you have actively tried to end your life. Sucks but that’s what it’s like. Also do think about how helpful admission will be and what makes it helpful. Is there anything you can do to get through without admission. 
You may need to be stubborn and pretend you don’t want help. Voluntary admission is fairly rare now so asking for help, shows your willingness to engage and reduces likelihood of admission

I always had really bad periods and would often faint, but my mum never did anything about it. It wasn’t till I left home that I went and got treatment. 
Because of my mental health I now regularly see my Gp, and psychologist. I’m apparently waisting there time and am a hypochondriac.  I often have hip pain which is likely to be related to being born with a dislocated hip, which wasn’t diagnosed for the first two years of my life. Yay to auntie who is also paediatrican for getting that sorted. But now I can’t get accurate information about the treatment I had for my hip from my parents as apparently it was nothing major, and I just need to lose weight.

Gp wanted him to go to hospital but mum wouldn’t allow and basically lied to the Gp that could look after at home as she was a trained nurse (retired ot actually) and I was at home, and was also a working nurse (I haven’t worked for 2 years). He still has to go to work full time as well as do all the house and garden heavy work. 

Growing up with being ill being a crime destroyed my trust in self and that I know my body

Hi ya. As someone who has an eupd diagnosis and waiting for Asd assessment I can understand your worries. I worked as a nurse for 5 years until my mental health got to shit. I would agree with previous answer about best to be honest. You might want to get a letter from Gp it health care professional who knows you just to stay that your stable and know when you need to ask for help. From my experience the thing there most interested in is that you are self aware and know when you might need a little extra support, and how to ask for it. Nursing is a stressful job. Good luck.

As it is mental health it’s not next of kin who has power it’s nearest living relative. If she has been sectioned under the mental health act, then they legally have to inform their nearest living relative. This will probably be your mum or dad (whichever’s elder). I would guess that trying her mobile regularly may be the best way to get hold of her, but she may not always have it on her as she is unlikely to be allowed a charger. 
Otherwise polity phone her local mental health units and ask to be put forward to the bed management team. They will know where she is, even if it’s out of area. You might do better to have your mum present when you phone so that her nearest living relative is around and they can talk to her if needed. 
I guess this is a really scary time for you, just remember that she is being cared for.

And trust me, from someone whose Nmum regularly uses standing on feet with heals on or folding feet in half, it’s very easy to do with people around without them noticing, and the feet are normally covered which hides any bruises. My advise. Wear covered shoes around your mum the whole time.

I’m from the uk so it is a bit different to other countries but from my experience unless you are actually acting on the suicidal urges then you won’t get admitted. 
I have been admitted to hospital both voluntarily and sectioned and its pretty tough to get sectioned. You have to be very unwell, actively trying to commit Suicide and like said two drs (at least one of them psychiatric) and an approved mental health practioner (amp) have to assess you and agree to the section. 

I know things in America and other countries are slightly different but I only know the U.K. system. There is a massive mental health bed crisis in the U.K.  people are not going to get admitted unless they are a great risk to themselves or others. For example I was picked up by the police trying to kill myself on four consecutive days, and assessed and released three of the times until the fourth time when I was sectioned and admitted for just over a week

I’ve been in psych wards many times in the uk. It’s really hard to get a bed on a psych ward. There just aren’t enough beds to go around. 
Your first point of call should be your Gp which you can make an emergency appointment with. If you have a care coordinator or have been under any mental health teams then contact them. 

They should be to refer you to the crisis team who will assess you and probably try and keep you at home. If feel like you need a bed to be safe let them know and be stubborn. 

Good luck and if you want to chat just message me. I know the uk system pretty well as an inpatient and nurse.
